steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules for building React components and managing state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components and managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main Kanban component
steps.instruction: Create a function component named KanbanBoard that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The component should be named KanbanBoard and return null.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Create the KanbanBoard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A KanbanBoard component function is created and returns null.
successCriteria: A function named KanbanBoard is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main KanbanBoard component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly KanbanBoard and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named KanbanBoard that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for columns
steps.instruction: Inside your KanbanBoard component, use useState to initialize state with three columns: 'todo', 'inProgress', and 'done'. Each column should be an array that will hold card objects.
steps.hint: Call useState with an object containing three keys, each set to an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have state ready to manage cards in three columns.
successCriteria: useState is called with an object containing 'todo', 'inProgress', and 'done' keys, each set to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the initial state structure for your Kanban board columns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an object that has exactly three keys: 'todo', 'inProgress', and 'done', each initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization doesn't match the expected structure. Use useState with an object containing three keys: 'todo', 'inProgress', and 'done', each set to an empty array.

steps.title: Initialize state for cards
steps.instruction: Inside your KanbanBoard component, use useState to initialize a state variable called 'cards' with sample data for three columns: 'To Do', 'In Progress', and 'Done'.
steps.hint: Create an array of card objects, each with an id, title, and column property. The column should match one of the three column names.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'cards' state variable containing sample card data for each column.
successCriteria: The 'cards' state is initialized with useState, containing at least one card object for each of the three columns.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the initial state for your Kanban cards.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the state initialization, but make sure to include sample cards for all three columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'cards' state isn't properly initialized. Check that you're using useState with an array of card objects.

steps.title: Create the moveCard handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your KanbanBoard component, create a function named moveCard that takes cardId and targetColumn as parameters. For now, just define the function signature and an empty body.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should be defined inside the component but before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: A moveCard function is defined inside the KanbanBoard component with two parameters: cardId and targetColumn.
successCriteria: The moveCard function is defined with the correct name and two parameters (cardId, targetColumn).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the moveCard handler function. This function will be responsible for moving cards between columns in our Kanban board.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named moveCard that takes two parameters: cardId and targetColumn.
steps.feedbackWrong: The moveCard function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named moveCard with two parameters (cardId, targetColumn) inside the KanbanBoard component.

steps.title: Implement moveCard logic
steps.instruction: Inside your moveCard function, implement the logic to update the cards state by filtering out the moved card from its current column and adding it to the target column.
steps.hint: You'll need to use setCards with a function that receives the current cards state, then return a new array that filters out the card from its current column and adds it to the target column.
steps.expectedOutcome: The moveCard function should properly update the cards state when called, removing the card from its current column and adding it to the target column.
successCriteria: The moveCard function uses setCards with a callback to update state, filters the card from its current column, and adds it to the target column.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the moveCard logic. The function now properly updates the cards state by moving cards between columns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your moveCard function properly updates the cards state. Make sure you're using setCards with a callback and correctly filtering/adding the card.
steps.feedbackWrong: The moveCard function doesn't properly update the cards state. Review the logic needed to filter the card from its current column and add it to the target column.

steps.title: Return the main container structure
steps.instruction: Return a div element with the className 'kanban-board' as the main container for your Kanban board.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that has the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with className 'kanban-board' as the main container.
successCriteria: The KanbanBoard component returns a div element with className 'kanban-board'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container for the Kanban board. This will hold all the columns and cards.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with exactly the className 'kanban-board'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main container structure isn't quite right. Remember to return a div with className 'kanban-board'.

steps.title: Map through columns to create column containers
steps.instruction: Inside the KanbanBoard component's return statement, map through the columns state to create a div for each column. Use the map method and return a div with a className of 'column' and a key prop set to the column name.
steps.hint:
Use columns.map(column =>
) inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The KanbanBoard component now renders a container div with three column divs inside, each representing a column from the columns state.
successCriteria: The columns state is mapped to create div elements with className='column' and proper key props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the columns to create dynamic column containers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the map method on the columns array and returning div elements with the correct className and key prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to use the map method on the columns array to create a div for each column with className='column' and key={column}.

steps.title: Display column titles
steps.instruction: Inside each column container, add an h3 element that displays the column name as its text content.
steps.hint: Place the h3 element inside the column div. Use the column variable from the map function to set the text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each column container will now display its name as a heading.
successCriteria: An h3 element is added inside each column div, displaying the column name as text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added titles to each column.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added an h3 element inside each column div with the column name as its content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added an h3 element inside the column divs with the correct column name.

steps.title: Map through cards to render card elements
steps.instruction: Inside the column container, after the column title, map through the cards that belong to that column to create individual card elements.
steps.hint: Use the filter method on the cards array to get cards for the current column, then map over them to create div elements with card content.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each column will display its title followed by a list of card elements for that column.
successCriteria: The column container includes a map over cards filtered by column, creating div elements with card content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the cards to render individual card elements within each column.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're filtering cards by the current column and creating proper card elements with content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cards aren't being rendered correctly. Check that you're filtering cards by column and mapping them to create div elements.

steps.title: Add move buttons to each card
steps.instruction: Inside the card mapping in your KanbanBoard component, add a button for moving cards to the next column. The button should call moveCard with the card's id, current column, and target column when clicked.
steps.hint: You can add a button element with an onClick handler. Inside the handler, call moveCard with appropriate arguments based on the current column index.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each card will have a button that triggers the moveCard function with appropriate parameters when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element is added inside the card mapping with an onClick handler that calls moveCard with card id, current column, and target column arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added move buttons to each card. The buttons are now wired to call the moveCard function with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it's inside the card mapping and calls moveCard with the required three arguments: card id, current column, and target column.
steps.feedbackWrong: The move buttons aren't properly implemented. Check that you've added button elements with onClick handlers that call moveCard with the correct parameters.

steps.title: Style the Kanban board with basic CSS
steps.instruction: Add a style object to the KanbanBoard component to style the board layout, columns, and cards with basic CSS properties.
steps.hint: Create a style object with properties like display, flexDirection, gap, border, padding, etc. Apply these styles to your JSX elements using the style attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The KanbanBoard component will have a style object with CSS properties for board layout, columns, and cards, ready to be applied to the JSX elements.
successCriteria: A style object is created with at least three CSS properties for board layout, columns, or cards.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a style object with CSS properties. This will help visualize the Kanban board layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure your style object includes at least three different CSS properties for the board, columns, or cards.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style object is missing or doesn't contain enough CSS properties. Try creating an object with properties like display, flexDirection, border, padding, or margin.
